project: Consolidate Factory Definitions Authored Loading and Validation
description: Publish one narrow Factory Definitions-owned capability that deterministically selects, loads, validates, and returns a detached authored Factory definition, then migrate one coherent Factory Runtime-facing loading path without changing live state ownership, Factory Sessions controls, Events, Recordings, packaged distribution, or generated transports.

context.customerAsk: Create and use a small Factory Definitions-owned authored-source and validation capability that supplies a selected, immutable, validated Factory definition. Keep authored loading and semantic validation in Factory Definitions, preserve current-directory and bundled/layout behavior and typed failure outcomes, and migrate one coherent Runtime-facing consumer without changing runtime state ownership or the D1/D2 boundaries.
context.problem: Factory Definitions currently exposes authored loading and validation through broad aggregate, mutable loaded-source, function-type, and compatibility contracts. Factory Runtime therefore lacks one focused public dependency guaranteeing deterministic selection and Definitions-owned validation, which invites excess authority, mutation aliasing, inconsistent failures, construction-time I/O, and future reach-through into Factory Sessions.
context.solution: Expose a focused Factory Definitions capability that accepts explicit selection context, composes the existing Definitions-owned source selection, authored decoding, split/bundled layout resolution, effective loading, and semantic validation, and returns a detached definition with typed failures. Construct it inertly through the owning provider and canonical wire graph, then inject it into one existing Runtime-facing loading path while leaving unrelated compatibility and all state, event, recording, distribution, and transport behavior unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria: Factory Definitions publishes a narrow authored-source and validation capability that accepts explicit selection context and returns one selected, detached, validated Factory definition without exposing implementation packages, validator collaborators, session handles, or unrelated Definitions operations.
Valid supported authored inputs preserve current-directory resolution, root-file precedence, split-layout and bundled-content behavior, effective base-directory semantics, and result immutability.

Missing input, malformed configuration, unresolved authored content, and blocking validation findings produce distinguishable actionable Factory Definitions-owned typed failures and never return a partial definition.

One coherent Runtime-facing loading path consumes only the declared public capability and preserves its successful and failing behavior without importing Definitions internals or reaching through Factory Sessions.

Capability construction performs no I/O, validation, materialization, caching, state mutation, or lifecycle activation; Runtime state ownership, Factory Session controls, Factory Events, Recordings JSONL history/replay, packaged distribution, and generated/public transports remain unchanged.
Quality gates pass: typecheck/Go compilation, formatting, lint, package-boundary checks, focused Factory Definitions and Runtime tests, make verify-fast, and the required CI tier.

Delivery continues through implementation and correctness-first review until required CI is terminal and passing, every blocking PR conversation is explicitly addressed, shared-file and merge conflicts are resolved, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Publish an inert focused capability
userStories.description: As a service consumer, I want a small Factory Definitions-owned loading and validation contract so that I can request a validated definition without receiving unrelated authority.
acceptanceCriteria: The public capability exposes one cohesive operation with plain Factory Definitions request, result, value, and typed-error vocabulary; request data does not contain filesystems, loaders, validators, loggers, Runtime types, or Factory Session types.
The success result contains only the selected source identity and detached effective-definition facts needed by the declared consumer.

Production composition constructs the capability once from explicit dependencies and injects it directly; no dependency bag, service locator, lazy constructor, child graph, or per-session service construction is introduced.

A construction test using observable fake effects proves construction performs no file reads/writes, validation, bundled-file materialization, caching, or lifecycle work before the operation is invoked.
Existing public compatibility entry points required by consumers outside this slice remain available; this story does not perform broad alias retirement.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: 2026-08-05: Published the process-scoped ValidatedAuthoredFactoryDefinitionLoader with one plain request/result operation and typed safe failure vocabulary. Canonical Wire constructs it once from the existing Definitions-owned loader and validator, Runtime Opening retains the exact inert instance, and focused tests prove construction performs no loading or validation while returned effective facts are detached. Focused Factory Definitions/Runtime tests, go vet, typecheck, and make verify-fast pass; repository pkg-file-count/pkg-boundary still report pre-existing baseline debt outside this story.

userStories.title: Load a deterministic immutable authored definition
userStories.description: As a Factory Runtime-facing consumer, I want valid authored inputs to resolve to the same detached effective definition so that representation and layout choices do not change Runtime intent.
acceptanceCriteria: Explicit JSON, YAML, and YML Factory files retain their supported decoding and selected-source identity behavior.

An explicit project/current directory retains existing current-Factory resolution, and a direct Factory directory retains the existing unambiguous factory.json, factory.yaml, or factory.yml root selection rules.

Split worker/workstation definitions, authored bodies/prompts, portable bundled files, starter content, and Runtime base-directory facts retain the existing accepted loading semantics applicable to the migrated path.
The operation applies the existing blocking structural/effective validation policy before returning success.
Mutating request bytes, loader-owned buffers, nested values in one returned result, or caller-local projections cannot change a retained result or a later result for unchanged authored input.
Focused Factory Definitions tests directly prove valid single-file, current/direct directory, split-layout, bundled-content, and mutation-isolation behavior.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: 2026-08-05: Preserved the concrete selected-root identity through compilation so the focused capability returns factory.json, factory.yaml, or factory.yml rather than the caller's directory. Added Definitions-owned behavioral coverage for explicit JSON/YAML/YML files, direct and current directory selection, split runtime bodies/prompts, bundled content materialization, runtime-base overrides, blocking validation, and nested result isolation. Focused race coverage, Factory Definitions packages, go vet, typecheck, and make verify-fast pass.

userStories.title: Return typed actionable load and validation failures
userStories.description: As a caller, I want loading and validation failures to remain specific and actionable so that I can distinguish configuration mistakes and stop before Runtime uses invalid state.
acceptanceCriteria: A missing selected source or directory without a supported definition returns a typed missing-definition outcome with safe source context and no partial success value.
Invalid JSON/YAML or content that cannot represent a Factory returns a typed malformed-definition outcome that preserves an inspectable cause without exposing authored payload contents.
Missing split definitions, unsafe or unresolved bundled/layout references, and other resolution failures remain distinguishable from syntax failures where the existing behavior distinguishes them.

Blocking structural or semantic findings return a typed validation failure with actionable existing finding fields; non-blocking warnings and hints retain the selected existing validation-profile behavior.
Cancellation and dependency failures preserve their cause and never return a usable definition.

Focused behavioral tests directly cover missing input, malformed configuration, unresolved authored content, blocking validation, non-blocking findings, and cancellation/dependency failure without meta-tests over files, methods, routes, or registrations.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: 2026-08-05: Classified the focused authored-loader's missing, malformed, unresolved, blocking-validation, and dependency outcomes while preserving typed sentinels and original inspectable causes. Source/layout and compilation boundaries now attach the stable failure classification at the operation that knows it, so the focused service does not infer meaning from error strings. Added real-loader coverage for missing files/directories, malformed JSON, missing split content, unsafe portable content, blocking findings, plus focused warning/hint, cancellation, and dependency behavior. Definitions tests, focused race coverage, go vet, typecheck, and make verify-fast pass.

userStories.title: Migrate one Runtime-facing loading path
userStories.description: As a Factory Runtime maintainer, I want one existing loading path to consume only the validated-definition capability so that Runtime receives trustworthy input through the intended ownership boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: One coherent existing Runtime-facing definition-loading path receives the focused capability directly through canonical construction and no longer receives separate broad loader or validator authority solely for that behavior.
Equivalent valid inputs produce the same selected Factory identity, effective definition, directories, split/bundled content, and Runtime construction outcome as before migration.
Missing, malformed, unresolved, and validation failures propagate with their typed classification and prevent Runtime construction from observing partial definition state.

The migrated consumer imports only public Factory Definitions contracts for this behavior and does not import Definitions internals, Factory Sessions internals, session registries, Runtime handles, response streams, or replacement-state types.
Focused integration and composition tests prove narrow direct injection, inert construction, valid loading, and representative typed failure propagation.

Regression evidence shows no change to mutable Runtime state ownership, Factory Session lifecycle or controls, invocation outcomes, Factory Event semantics, Recordings snapshots/history/replay, packaged distribution, or transport/generated contracts.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: 2026-08-05: Migrated live Factory Session Runtime opening to LoadRuntimeFromDefinition, which passes explicit selection context to the process-scoped ValidatedAuthoredFactoryDefinitionLoader and rebuilds the existing mutable Runtime source only from its detached result. Current-Factory resolution and blocking validation now stay in Factory Definitions; Runtime preserves selected root identity, effective config, directories, bundled replacement facts, base directory, replay behavior, and typed loading failures without invoking the legacy authored loader. Focused race/owner tests, Factory Sessions/Definitions/Wire suites, go vet, generated wire, and make verify-fast pass. make lint reaches only 90 pre-existing backend-size violations outside this change; the changed packages do not appear in that report.
